Hi Maya — thanks, brief answers below and a proposed pattern. Kim and Marissa are looped in for acceptance criteria and runbook items.

Summary recommended pattern (high level):
- Local sidecar (lightweight) on inference hosts for immediate prefix/KV caching and scrub hooks -> forward to a VPC-local HEC proxy (reverse proxy with mTLS termination and token exchange) -> outbound HEC endpoint in customer-managed Splunk or a Splunk Cloud Gateway.
- Rationale: sidecars reduce tail-latency by doing local buffering and apply scrub rules before any network egress; the HEC proxy centralizes auth, auditing, and rate-limiting and simplifies firewall rules.

Transport and formats:
- Preferred: Splunk HEC over HTTPS with mutual TLS.
- Alternatives: syslog over TLS to a central forwarder that translates to HEC (supported but more configuration).

Scrubbing tiers and chain-of-custody:
- Three scrub levels we propose: 
  1) minimal (token masking only) — for high-fidelity debugging;
  2) standard (PII redaction + token masking) — recommended for customer-facing telemetry;
  3) strict (hashing/anonymization + schema pruning) — for regulated workloads.
- Sidecar applies scrub before any network transmit; HEC proxy emits an immutable delivery receipt with timestamp + sidecar checksum for chain-of-custody.

Evidence and retention:
- We'll provide a sample evidence bundle: delivery receipts, proxy audit log extract, example scrubbed/un-scrubbed sample pairs (anonymized), and a short runbook. Retention configurable — common defaults: 90 / 365 / 730 days depending on account SLA.

Next steps:
- I'll attach an architecture sketch and an evidence checklist for review.
- Can your security team confirm the preferred retention tier and whether they require on-disk encryption for sidecar cache?

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 11:04 AM Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Summary recommended pattern (high level):
> - Local sidecar ... -> forward to a VPC-local HEC proxy ...

Couple of technical clarifications from the runtime side:

- Ports & firewall: the sidecar only needs outbound HTTPS (443) to the HEC proxy. The proxy will accept mTLS on 8443 internally; if customers prefer, we can flip to 443 as well. We'll document minimum Security Group rules.
- Sampling & traces: traces are emitted by the runtime; the sidecar can add an "exported_by" tag and a trace-hash header. For high-volume customers we suggest client-side sampling at the sidecar with deterministic sampling keys to preserve representativeness.
- KV cache persistence: by default the cache is ephemeral (in-memory + short disk spill). For accounts requiring full reproduce logs we can enable encrypted disk persistence (LUKS) — this has operational cost.
- Delivery receipts: proxy will return a JSON receipt with sequence id, timestamp (RFC3339), and SHA256 of the payload. We'll include an example in the evidence bundle.

I'll add firewall snippet and an example receipt to the Confluence page linked below.

-Jonas

Sofia / Kimberly,

Appreciate the proposed pattern. A few audit-specific clarifications before we proceed to a POC: 

1) PII proof: we need a sample record that demonstrates redaction at the sidecar and the corresponding audit receipt showing parity (i.e., we need to be able to show auditors that raw PII never left our VPC).
2) Time sync: receipts must show monotonicity for a sequence of events. Do you recommend we use NTP + proxy-side reconcile window?
3) Third-party access: Splunk SE is on copy — will the proxy permit Splunk-managed ingestion if we lease Splunk Cloud? Any differences in the receipt format?

Also, we saw mentions of on-disk encrypted caches. For SOC 2 we strongly prefer no persistent copies of raw payloads on disk; if caching is required we need it to be encrypted and auto-expiring.

Can you provide the sample artifacts and a short statement we can present to the auditor?

Regards,
Leah Kim
Security Engineer, Globex Corp

Leah / Team — thanks, below is an actionable plan and a delivery timeline.

Actionable plan:
1) Provide sample evidence bundle (attached) that includes: 
   - example raw record (sanitized for obvious PII) + the sidecar-redacted output;
   - proxy delivery receipt examples (sequence id, RFC3339 timestamp, SHA256).
   - a short one-page auditor statement describing sidecar scrub guarantees and chain-of-custody.
2) Configure sidecar in "standard" scrub mode (PII redaction + token masking) for the POC; no persistent raw payloads on disk. If you require a reproduce mode later we can enable encrypted ephemeral cache with a 24-hour TTL.
3) Time sync: recommend NTP with proxy reconcile tolerance of 5s; receipts include agent timestamp + proxy-validated timestamp. We'll include monotonic sequence numbers for event windows.
4) Splunk Cloud: proxy can forward to either Splunk Cloud HEC or a customer-managed Splunk; receipt format is identical. Splunk-managed solutions may add additional ingestion metadata but we keep receipt parity.

- Today (Nov 27): sample evidence bundle + auditor statement (attached).
